title: A date on a piece of paper
body: You are Elena, a fictional parent living with your eight-year-old daughter, Lucía. Your protection application is already filed. A hearing notice arrives. You have $900, unstable housing, and twelve weeks to prepare. The notice is in English. Your next shift begins in an hour.
learn: A notice creates obligations even when its language is unfamiliar. This story begins after filing and does not teach asylum eligibility or filing deadlines.

choices.label: Ask a community interpreter to read it with you
choices.consequence: You write the hearing details in a calendar. A volunteer helps you make a list of questions.

choices.label: Pay for help reading the notice
choices.consequence: You understand the date, location, and instructions, but lose money needed for the week.

choices.label: Ask a friend after your shift
choices.consequence: Your friend explains the date but cannot answer legal questions. You keep the original notice.

title: The address on the envelope
body: Your cousin can no longer host you. A room is available, but the deposit is $300. Every move makes mail and transportation harder.
learn: The court must be told when contact information changes. Informing a different agency does not necessarily update the court.

choices.label: Rent the room and arrange help updating your court address
choices.consequence: You secure a room and get help completing the court address update.

choices.label: Stay temporarily with another family and ask them to hold your mail
choices.consequence: You save the deposit. You still need to update the court and keep checking for mail.

choices.label: Ask a community group for emergency housing
choices.consequence: In this fictional community, a short-term room becomes available after a week of calls. Availability is not guaranteed elsewhere.

title: The calls no one answers
body: Three legal-service organizations have waiting lists. A private consultation costs $120. A stranger promises a guaranteed result for cash.
learn: You can seek qualified representation at no expense to the government. A legal-service directory is a starting point; being listed does not mean an organization can accept every case.

choices.label: Keep calling qualified nonprofit providers
choices.consequence: A clinic schedules a screening. It has not agreed to represent you.

choices.label: Pay for a consultation with a licensed attorney
choices.consequence: The attorney explains next steps. A consultation alone does not establish ongoing representation.

choices.label: Decline the guarantee and use the official provider directory
choices.consequence: You avoid the promise of a guaranteed outcome and identify qualified providers.

title: A document across an ocean
body: A relative may have a hospital record relevant to what happened before you left. Calling repeatedly could draw unwanted attention to them. A copy service asks $90.
learn: Evidence must be evaluated in context. If corroboration cannot reasonably be obtained, explaining why can matter. A missing record is not proof that an event did not occur.

choices.label: Ask your relative once, through a safer contact
choices.consequence: A partial copy arrives. Some dates are difficult to read. You preserve what you received.

choices.label: Pay for retrieval through a trusted contact
choices.consequence: A clearer copy arrives in this story. Paying for retrieval does not guarantee that records exist or can be safely obtained.

choices.label: Do not expose your relative; document why the record is unavailable
choices.consequence: You write down the danger, your attempts, and what other evidence might be available.

title: The missed call
body: Your phone plan expires just as the clinic calls. Your daughter needs groceries. Both feel urgent.
learn: A missed callback may reflect money, connectivity, work, or childcare. It does not establish indifference to the case.

choices.label: Pay $40 for phone access
choices.consequence: You reconnect with the clinic and confirm its appointment.

choices.label: Buy groceries and call from the library
choices.consequence: Your daughter eats. Library hours and a shared phone make the callback harder.

choices.label: Ask a community worker to arrange a safe callback
choices.consequence: You agree on a time and a contact method that does not expose personal details to others.

title: Tell the story again
body: At a clinic screening, an interpreter joins. You remember an important event but cannot place it on an exact date. Your daughter is waiting in the hallway.
learn: Interpretation and document translation are different tasks. A careful interview can distinguish an uncertain date from an uncertain event.

choices.label: Explain what you remember and where you are uncertain
choices.consequence: The interviewer separates confirmed facts from estimates and makes space for a follow-up.

choices.label: Ask for a second appointment with childcare arranged
choices.consequence: You have more time to explain the sequence. In this story, the clinic can schedule another appointment.

choices.label: Use your own timeline and ask the interpreter to clarify unfamiliar words
choices.consequence: The timeline includes approximate dates and questions. You do not invent details to fill gaps.

title: A record you cannot afford to translate
body: You have a short medical record in Spanish. A qualified translator quotes $100. A friend offers an informal summary.
learn: Foreign-language documents submitted in immigration court require an English translation with the appropriate certification. A summary is different from a complete translation.

choices.label: Pay for a complete certified translation
choices.consequence: The record and translation can be reviewed together. Cost does not decide its legal weight.

choices.label: Ask the clinic about volunteer translation
choices.consequence: In this story, a volunteer completes the translation after a delay. This resource may not be available in every community.

choices.label: Keep the original and explain the translation gap to qualified help
choices.consequence: You preserve the record and flag what remains incomplete rather than treating a summary as a certified translation.

title: Two appointments. One afternoon.
body: Your daughter has a medical appointment on the afternoon of a case-preparation meeting. Missing work again threatens the household budget.
learn: Scheduling pressure can affect a case long before the hearing. A practical support plan is part of understanding the client’s circumstances.

choices.label: Arrange childcare and attend the preparation meeting
choices.consequence: You attend. The cost leaves less for transportation and food.

choices.label: Ask the clinic to reschedule and take your daughter to the doctor
choices.consequence: The meeting moves in this story. The delay narrows the time left to prepare.

choices.label: Ask for a shorter phone appointment after the doctor
choices.consequence: You discuss the urgent issues, but some documents need a later review.

title: What belongs in the file?
body: Your folder contains copies, a timeline, translation notes, and a list of missing records. The court’s instructions include a filing date specific to this case.
learn: A court’s filing instructions matter. This story does not substitute a universal deadline for the instructions governing a real case.

choices.label: Ask qualified help to review the packet against the instructions
choices.consequence: In this story, a volunteer checks organization and identifies remaining questions. This is not a promise of representation.

choices.label: Pay $45 for copies and organize the packet yourself
choices.consequence: You retain a copy and keep track of what was submitted. Some legal questions remain.

choices.label: Prioritize the required items and explain missing material
choices.consequence: You distinguish unavailable evidence from items still being prepared and seek help on the unresolved issues.

title: The last bus
body: The hearing is approaching. Transportation, childcare, and a night of lost sleep are now part of the case. You have the hearing notice in your folder.
learn: Getting to court can require planning around childcare and transit. In real proceedings, failing to appear can have serious consequences; qualified advice and current court information matter.

choices.label: Reserve transport and childcare
choices.consequence: You have a confirmed plan and a backup contact.

choices.label: Arrange a volunteer ride
choices.consequence: A volunteer agrees in this fictional community. You confirm the details rather than assuming a ride will arrive.

choices.label: Take the early bus with your daughter
choices.consequence: You arrive tired and early. Your daughter waits beside you.

title: When your name is called
body: You reach the hearing. The judge, the government attorney, and an interpreter have different roles. The clinic’s help with paperwork did not mean it would appear as your attorney.
learn: The respondent and DHS are parties to removal proceedings. The immigration judge is part of EOIR in the Department of Justice. Court interpretation does not replace legal representation.

choices.label: Ask the interpreter to clarify what you did not understand
choices.consequence: The instruction is repeated. You explain the factual questions and remaining gaps without pretending to understand.

choices.label: Request more time to seek representation or complete preparation
choices.consequence: You state why more time is needed. A request is not automatically granted. This prototype follows an illustrative continued-hearing branch.

choices.label: Proceed with your organized folder and explain what is missing
choices.consequence: The hearing proceeds in this fictional case. Legal eligibility and the complete record—not a game score—govern a real decision.

title: Life after the hearing
body: The hearing ends, but your daughter still needs dinner, the room still needs rent, and your relatives still ask when you will know.
learn: The prototype’s endings are authored teaching examples. Costs, time, support, and evidence indicators are fictional; they are not approval probabilities, legal tests, or predictions.

choices.label: Make a plan for the next notice and follow-up
choices.consequence: You keep copies, confirm a safe contact method, and plan how to obtain qualified help with what happens next.

choices.label: Rest with your daughter before the next round of calls
choices.consequence: A short pause does not erase your effort. The case and the pressures on your household remain.
